name: Outdoor Cinema: Sing Street
why: Outdoor screening of the 2016 Irish musical drama Sing Street.

name: The Namesake 20th Anniversary Screening
why: Free outdoor screening of Mira Nair's 2006 film The Namesake in its 20th anniversary year.

name: Taste of Times Square

name: Gather Round: Let's Dance at Manhattan West

name: Paper Cuts: Independent Publishing in the US, 2000–2025

name: Stew: AIR 17 Final Exhibition
why: Final exhibition of works by eight artists completing Textile Arts Center's 17th artist residency program.

name: Beastie Boys Square Tribute Art Show
why: Open call group art show celebrating the third anniversary of the naming of Beastie Boys Square at the Lower East Side gallery.

name: Ridgewood Off-Kilter Film Festival
venue: Stone Circle Theatre / Trinity Reformed Church / Footlight Underground
why: Community-driven film festival screening feature films, animated and live-action shorts, documentaries, and music videos by NYC, domestic, and international filmmakers.

name: 12th Annual Brooklyn Americana Music Festival
venue: DUMBO Archway and venues in DUMBO / Red Hook / Carroll Gardens
why: Folk, roots, and country blues across DUMBO, Red Hook, and Carroll Gardens, with 20+ artists on multiple stages.

name: US Open for All
venue: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center
why: Free public access day at the US Open grounds, including men's doubles semifinals, women's singles semifinals, wheelchair events, and junior quarterfinals.

name: DapperQ 11th Annual NYFW LGBTQIA+ Fashion Show

name: Bryant Park Picnic Performances: Dance Party All-Stars
why: Free outdoor performance featuring the Alfredo de la Fé All Star Band and George Gee Swing Orchestra; blankets and bistro chairs provided.

name: Comedians Interview Experts: Ignorance & Science
why: Comedian Ike Ufomadu interviews neuroscientist Dr. Stuart Firestein on how ignorance, not knowledge, drives scientific discovery.

name: Comedians Interview Experts: Measuring Consciousness
why: Comedian Asher Pearlman interviews Dr. Weiji Ma on the science and challenge of measuring consciousness.

name: Comedians Interview Experts: Psychology of Spirituality
why: Padma Lakshmi interviews Dr. Lisa Miller on the psychology of spirituality and its connection to human flourishing.

name: Comedians Interview Experts: The Craft of Puzzles
why: Comedian Negin Farsad interviews crossword constructor Wyna Liu on the art and craft of puzzle-making.

name: Comedians Interview Experts: Checking Health Claims
why: Ophira Eisenberg interviews Dr. Andrea Love on how to separate credible health advice from wellness industry bullshit.

name: Lesbian Renaissance: A Medieval Themed Lavender Market
why: A medieval-themed queer market featuring vendors, community, and a lavender aesthetic at a Bed-Stuy café.

name: Brazilian Independence Day Fest
why: Outdoor street festival celebrating Brazilian Independence Day on Astoria's open street.

name: 46th Annual Richmond County Fair
why: Annual county fair at Historic Richmond Town on Staten Island, running through Labor Day.

name: 59th Annual West Indian Day Parade
venue: Eastern Parkway (Utica Ave to Grand Army Plaza)
source: West Indian American Day Carnival Association
why: Annual Labor Day Caribbean carnival parade along Eastern Parkway, celebrating West Indian culture with music, costumes, and street food.

name: West Side County Fair
why: Free waterfront county fair at Riverside Park on the Hudson River.

name: Brailed It (Documentary)
why: Documentary following blind and low-vision kids at the annual Braille Challenge competition; audio description is woven into the storytelling. Q+A with filmmakers on 9/4–9/5.

name: Public Works' Public Record
why: 100+ New Yorkers join musicians and dancers at the Delacorte to create a live album in real time; the resulting recording will be preserved at NYPL. Free tickets via in-person or digital lottery.

name: Metropolitan Opera Summer HD Festival
why: Encore screenings from the Met's Live in HD series projected onto the opera house façade at Lincoln Center Plaza; 2,500 seats available first come, first served.

name: Cake Zine at Little Island
why: James Beard Award-winning literary food magazine Cake Zine curates a reading series at Little Island about the past, present, and future of NYC's food scene, followed by an open writing group.

name: 27th Annual Tromadance Film Festival
why: Troma Entertainment's annual celebration of outrageous, low-budget filmmaking with screenings, drag, and bingo over three nights.

name: Molière in the Park: Don Juan
venue: Lefrak Center at Lakeside, Prospect Park
why: Free outdoor theater production of Molière's Don Juan — a tale of desire, power, and hypocrisy — with a live cello score, running through September 27 at Prospect Park's Lefrak Center.

name: Melofest 2026
why: Two-year anniversary celebration of Melophobe, a Bushwick DIY music space, with back-to-back bands and DJs across two stages, an ambient room, casino games, a bouncy house, and vendors.

name: Tom D's Big New York Show
why: Comedian and licensed NYC tour guide Tom Delgado covers NYC history, comedy, and trivia; this month features visual artist and historian John Vasquez Mejias on the Puerto Rican War.

name: Free Show Brain Concert at Tompkins Square Park
why: Free outdoor concert at Tompkins Square Park featuring Sid Simons, 95 Bulls, Dauber, and more.

name: Union Pool Summer Thunder Concert Series
why: Free daytime backyard concert closing the season with Heavy Blanket (feat. J Mascis), Crickets (JD Samson, Roddy Bottum, Michael O'Neill), and Tami Hart.

name: Movie Musical Mondays: Singin' in the Rain
why: Classic 1952 musical Singin' in the Rain, starring Gene Kelly, Debbie Reynolds, and Donald O'Connor, on the big screen as part of the annual Movie Musical Mondays series.

name: Ars Nova ANT Fest
why: Annual 'All New Talent' festival showcasing new theater, music, and hybrid performance work over two weeks at Ars Nova.

name: Risk! Live Show and Story Slam
why: Kevin Allison's Risk! show where guests tell true stories they never thought they'd share in public; this edition includes a mini-story slam with audience members.

name: The Femmes: Gay Prom
why: Queer prom night with live music by The Femmes, an all-woman and nonbinary party band playing songs by female and nonbinary artists.

name: We Will Always Love You: A Dolly Parton Celebration
why: Live concert by cover band Doll Parts, celebrating Dolly Parton's greatest hits.

name: Scream Scene Horror Hangout: Tales from the Hood
why: Free screening of Rusty Cundieff's 1995 horror anthology Tales from the Hood.

name: Carly Rae Jepsen Night
why: Dance night dedicated to the full Carly Rae Jepsen catalog — hits, deep cuts, B-sides, and new singles.

name: Bryant Park Picnic Performances: Brass Festival
why: Bryant Park's first-ever brass festival featuring New Brass Band, Brass Queens, and Aberdeen blending traditional brass with R&B, pop, and soul.

name: Lower East Stories Storytelling Salon
why: Monthly storytelling salon with a fresh theme; this month's theme is 'class.'

name: Bryant Park Fall Migration Birding Tours
why: Guided walks with urban naturalist Gabriel Willow discovering bird diversity during fall migration through Bryant Park.

name: Rooftop Cinema Club: September Screenings
why: Open-sky rooftop screenings of cult favorites, classics, and new releases through September, including Amélie, Casablanca, Get Out, Hocus Pocus, Sinners, and more; wireless headphones included.

name: Woven Together: Touch Exhibition
why: Annual community exhibition of tactile fiber art by artists from the disability arts community — works are soft, textured, weighty, smooth, and meant to be experienced through touch.

name: Teenage Malady Screening Series
why: Mini screening series exploring the darker side of adolescence, featuring River's Edge, The Virgin Suicides, Elephant, and Totally F***ed Up.

name: The New York Groove Live: Labor Days Edition
why: Independent journalist-led show mixing newsmakers and comedians about how to be a better New Yorker; this edition dives into the history of organized labor in NYC with Liz Haynes and Hamilton Nolan.

name: Sunset Salsa
why: Salsa dance lessons followed by a live performance by People of Earth at the downtown waterfront.

name: Sagematch: Scientists vs. Comedians
why: Scientists and comedians compete head-to-head creating and delivering impromptu presentations based on audience-suggested topics.

name: 9th Rockaway Film Festival
why: Five days of independent films, shorts, live music, and filmmaker Q+As; highlights include a documentary with live music by TV on the Radio's Kyp Malone and a film from How to with John Wilson's creator.

name: Morningside Lights Lantern-Building Workshops
why: Create giant lanterns for the 15th annual Morningside Lights procession on September 19; no experience needed.

name: Morningside Lights Procession
why: The 15th annual community lantern procession illuminating Morningside Heights with dozens of giant handmade lanterns.

name: SummerStage: Samara Joy, Christian McBride & Verve 70th Anniversary
why: Free SummerStage concert celebrating Verve Records' 70th anniversary with Samara Joy and Christian McBride, Mei Semones + friends playing Getz/Gilberto, and a DJ set by Sparklmami.

name: 17th Annual NYC Unicycle Festival
why: Annual unicycle festival with long-distance rides across the Brooklyn Bridge and to Coney Island, plus games, demonstrations, and a learn-to-ride area in Jackson Heights.

name: The Cultural Center at St. John's: ETHEL String Quartet
source: The Cultural Center at St. John's
why: Greenpoint's St. John's Lutheran Church inaugurates its new cultural and performing arts center with Grammy-winning string quartet ETHEL.

name: Bryant Park Picnic Performances: Grace Kelly & Ashni
why: Free outdoor performance presented by Asian American Arts Alliance featuring R&B, electropop, and smooth jazz from Grace Kelly and Ashni.

name: Infinite Good Times Movie Club: Demolition Man
why: Free screening of Demolition Man (1993) at a Gowanus metal bar, with pre-show trivia and free popcorn.

name: GPT-6 Astra Hackathon NYC
why: Build with GPT-6 Astra at Cerebral Valley and OpenAI's official hackathon; compete for $100,000 in OpenAI credits, a year of ChatGPT Pro, and OpenAI DevDay 2026 tickets. Teams of up to four; application required.

name: Claude & Coffee NYC
why: After-work coworking and networking gathering for founders, developers, operators, and AI enthusiasts building with AI.

name: Daytona AI Builders NYC – September 2026
why: Live demo showing how to fine-tune a small code model via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) so it learns from mistakes in isolated sandboxes — practical RL for code generation.

name: MongoDB.local NYC: For Founders Building What's Next
why: MongoDB's NYC community day with technical sessions, live demos, and founder networking around intelligent-data apps; MongoDB for Startups founders get free access plus Atlas credits and Voyage AI tokens.

name: The Harness Engineering & Model Wrangling Hackathon
why: One-day NYC hackathon to build persistent, adaptive AI agents using MongoDB Atlas, Vector Search, and Agentic Memory; finalists showcase projects live at MongoDB.local NYC on September 30.

name: Terms of Agreement 🐳
why: Jonas Lund and Yoshi Sodeoka's commission for MoMI's Schlosser Media Wall tracks real-time wallet transactions of major NFT 'whale' collectors alongside live GPS data from actual whales at sea.

name: MoMI LAB
time: Thu 2–6 PM, Fri 2–8 PM, Sat–Sun 11 AM–6 PM (ongoing)
why: Drop-in interactive experiences and deep-learning stations exploring emerging technologies and the moving image, facilitated by Museum educators.

name: Gordon Matta-Clark: Conversation on Walls Paper
why: Jessamyn Fiore, Director of the Estate of Gordon Matta-Clark, joins scholar Frances Richard for a public conversation on Matta-Clark's relationship to books and language, on occasion of the 'New Openings Against Old Surfaces' exhibition.

name: New Openings Against Old Surfaces: Gordon Matta-Clark's Walls Paper
why: The first exhibition focused on Gordon Matta-Clark's publishing output, centered on his 1973 artists' book Walls Paper — photographs abstracting demolished tenement interiors in the South Bronx and Lower East Side — presented on Printed Matter's 50th anniversary.

name: Governors Island Monthly Tree Tour
why: Monthly guided tree tour exploring the ecology and history of the trees on Governors Island.

name: LMCC Open Studios at Governors Island
price: Free (ferry fare $5 adults, free for many)
why: Public open house in the workspaces of LMCC's 2026 Arts Center Residents cohort, with artist activations including hands-on art-making, a listening experience, and a work-in-progress performance.

name: NYCRuns Endless Summer 10K at Governors Island
why: End-of-summer 10K race around Governors Island, one of the city's most scenic running routes.

name: Governors Island: Late Summer Evenings
time: Open until 10 PM Sun–Thu and 11 PM Fri–Sat through Labor Day (Sep 7)
price: Free (ferry $5 round-trip adults; free some weekends before 11 AM)
why: Final weeks of late-night summer hours with sunset views and late-night food vendors; ferry service until 10–11 PM through Labor Day.

name: Inside the Public Design Commission Archive: NYC's Design Review Agency
why: Rare access to the archive of the agency that reviews all permanent public art and structures on NYC-owned property.

name: Rare Look Inside M&S Schmalberg: NYC's Last Custom Fabric Flower Factory
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the last factory in NYC still making custom silk and fabric flowers by hand, supplying the fashion and theater industries since 1930.

name: After-Hours Pastel Painting Workshop @ AKC Museum of the Dog
why: After-hours pastel painting workshop in the American Kennel Club Museum of the Dog, surrounded by historic dog portraiture and breed art.

name: Private Lawn Bowling Workshop @ Central Park's New York Lawn Bowling Club
venue: NY Lawn Bowling Club, Central Park
why: Private introduction to lawn bowling — a sport with roots in 17th-century New Amsterdam — on the hidden greens of Central Park's NYC Lawn Bowling Club.

name: Rosé & Chocolate Tasting @ Roni-Sue's Secret Backyard
why: Wine and chocolate pairing tasting in the hidden backyard of the legendary LES chocolatier Roni-Sue's.

name: Exclusive After-Hours Tour @ The United Nations Headquarters
why: After-hours access to the UN Headquarters chambers, art, and history, timed to coincide with the 81st UN General Assembly session.

name: Exploring the World Trade Center Site: From Oculus to 9/11 Memorial
why: Guided walk through the World Trade Center complex exploring the history, architecture, and meaning of the rebuilt site, from Santiago Calatrava's Oculus to the 9/11 Memorial pools.

name: Exploring Andy Warhol & Truman Capote's Upper East Side
why: Walking tour tracing the UES haunts and homes of Andy Warhol and Truman Capote during the golden years of New York glamour.

name: The Secret Eats of Chinatown, Manhattan Food Crawl
why: Food crawl through the oldest and most storied blocks of Chinatown, sampling dim sum, roast meats, boba, and street food from family-run spots most visitors never find.

name: Exploring the Seaside Village of City Island
why: Guided walk through the quirky nautical village in the Bronx that feels like a small New England fishing town — sailboat yards, seafood shacks, and a storied America's Cup history.

name: Taverns of Early New York: A Walk Through Colonial Drinking Culture
why: Walking tour tracing the history of colonial-era taverns in lower Manhattan — centers of politics, business, and rebellion that shaped the early city.

name: Exploring Brooklyn Heights: Authors, Abolitionism, and Amazing Views
why: Walking tour of one of NYC's most storied neighborhoods — home to Walt Whitman's printers, abolitionist meeting houses, and the Promenade overlooking lower Manhattan.

name: Look Up! The Hidden History of NYC's Wooden Water Towers
why: Walking tour looking up at the rooftop wooden water towers that define the Manhattan skyline — their history, construction, and the family-run businesses still making them.

name: Exploring the Grand Mansions & Hidden Histories of Park Slope
why: Walking tour of Park Slope's Gilded Age brownstone mansions and the hidden stories of the industrialists, reformers, and artists who built the neighborhood.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building: NYC's Cathedral of Commerce
why: Exclusive access to the lobby and upper floors (including 26th floor) of Cass Gilbert's 1913 neo-Gothic skyscraper, once the tallest building in the world.

name: Behind the Scenes @ Fulton Fish Market: World's 2nd Largest Fish Market
why: Rare early-morning behind-the-scenes tour of the Fulton Fish Market before it opens, plus the opportunity to buy wholesale-quality fish directly from vendors — a bucket-list NYC experience.

name: Inside The Players w/ Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Untouched Bedroom
why: Rare access to The Players — the private arts club founded by Edwin Booth in 1888 — including Booth's personal bedroom, which remains preserved exactly as he left it at his death in 1893.

name: The Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue Food Crawl: The Bronx's Little Italy
why: Food crawl through the Bronx's authentic Italian-American commercial strip — fresh pasta, handmade mozzarella, pastries, and imports at family-run delis and markets.

name: Speakeasies & Swing Street: Exploring NYC's Prohibition Nightlife History
why: Walking tour through the jazz clubs, speakeasies, and Swing-era venues that defined Manhattan nightlife during Prohibition and the 1930s.

name: The Garbage That Built New York: A Walk Through NYC's Trash & Rat History
why: Walking tour exploring the history of garbage, public health crises, and rat infestations that literally shaped the city's geography — much of Lower Manhattan is built on landfill.

name: East Village, Rocks! Exploring the Neighborhood's Rock Music Legacy
why: Walking tour through the East Village's rock and punk music history — the clubs, crash pads, and stages that launched Blondie, Television, Richard Hell, and the Ramones.

name: Exploring the Gilded Age Mansions and Memorials of Riverside Drive
why: Walking tour along Riverside Drive's Gilded Age row of mansion apartments, war memorials, and the stunning Grant's Tomb.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Lincoln Center: Extended Tour Inside Iconic Halls
why: Extended backstage tour of Lincoln Center's concert halls, opera house, and backstage areas — including the Met Opera, David Geffen Hall, and Alice Tully Hall.

name: Exclusive Truffle 101 & Hands-On Tasting @ The Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Truffle education and tasting session at the NYC outpost of Urbani, the world's largest truffle supplier, covering truffle varieties, hunting, and pairings.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Ferry tour along the East River revealing the hidden infrastructure of the city — power plants, water tunnels, bridges, and the industrial history visible only from the water.

name: Exploring Greenwich Village's Music History: From Dylan to Springsteen
why: Walking tour of the coffeehouses, clubs, and crash pads in Greenwich Village that shaped American folk and rock music, from Bob Dylan's early years to Bruce Springsteen's breakthrough.

name: Unlocking Private Gilded Age Mausoleums @ Woodlawn Cemetery
why: Guided tour with private access inside the locked mausoleums of the Gilded Age elite at Woodlawn Cemetery, resting place of Miles Davis, Herman Melville, and dozens of New York's wealthiest dynasties.

name: Exploring the Ghosts of New York City's Elevated Railroads
why: Walking tour tracing the ghost infrastructure of Manhattan's demolished elevated train lines — the pillars, shadows, and memory of the old 'Els' still visible in the streetscape.

name: From Paris to New York: Exploring the Upper East Side's Fashion Legacy
why: Walking tour exploring the haute couture boutiques, atelier addresses, and socialite apartments that made the Upper East Side the American capital of European fashion.

name: The Occupied City: New York and the American Revolution
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Major exhibition framing the American Revolution as a story of civic choice, tracing New York's role from the first sparks of rebellion in 1763 to its emergence as the new nation's first capital in 1790.

name: Public Art as Public Health: The Role of Visual Art in Hospitals
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Panel drawing on the Hospital Murals Evaluation — the largest international study of murals in hospitals — tracing a through line from WPA-commissioned art and Keith Haring's gift to Woodhull Hospital to evidence-informed care environments being built today.

name: AIA New York Architecture Boat Tours
why: Two-hour guided boat tours of New York Harbor and the waterfront led by licensed architects, exploring the city's skyline, bridges, and waterfront development.

name: AIA NY Climate Change, Architecture, and the Future of NYC Tour
why: Boat tour examining how sea-level rise, storm surge, and climate adaptation are reshaping NYC's waterfront architecture and infrastructure, from flood barriers to elevated parks.

name: AIA NY Industrial Waterway Tour to Freshkills Park
why: Boat tour along Staten Island's industrial waterways to Freshkills Park, the former landfill being transformed into one of NYC's largest new parks — twice the size of Central Park.

name: Fort Greene Park Jazz Festival
venue: Fort Greene Park (Monument Plaza, West Wing)
why: Annual free neighborhood jazz festival in the park, running since 2010, with live performances in the shadow of the Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument.

name: Black History & Culture Tour of Fort Greene: Heart of Black Fort Greene (Fulton Street)
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at DeKalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Walking tour led by local historian Suzanne Spellen exploring Fort Greene's deep roots in Black history — from the 1800s to today — developed with BlackSpace, MoCADA, and Weeksville Heritage Center.

name: America's 250th Anniversary Tour of Fort Greene Park
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at DeKalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Walking tour tracing Fort Greene's role in the American Revolutionary War — the Battle of Brooklyn, the founding of the park, and the legacy of prison ship martyrs — with local historians as part of Brooklyn 250.

name: Moomin Celebration Day at NYBG
why: Final day of the Summer of Moomin at NYBG, celebrated with a special afternoon featuring a film screening, panel discussion with The Marginalian's Maria Popova and author Kate Zambreno, plus nature walks, sketching sessions, and flower crown making.

name: Flower Power at the New York Botanical Garden
why: Botanical art exhibition drawing on floral symbolism in pop culture, featuring work by artist Eugenia Mello alongside NYBG's second peak rose bloom, dahlia display, and Native Plant Garden meadow.

name: Coppola: A 25-Film Retrospective at Film Forum
why: Final days of a 25-film career retrospective of Francis Ford Coppola — The Godfather I-III, Apocalypse Now, The Conversation, Rumble Fish, and more — closing September 10.

name: Big + Loud! Film Series at The Paris Theater
why: Epic 70mm and large-format film series through Sep 15 — Lawrence of Arabia, West Side Story, The Sound of Music, Boogie Nights, Die Hard, and more on the biggest screen in midtown.

name: Dream Up Festival at Theater for the New City
why: 14th annual festival of new works — 23 productions including 18 world premieres — at the beloved community theater space in the East Village, running through September 16.

name: North Brooklyn Community Boathouse Free Canoeing
why: Free community paddle on Newtown Creek in a 29-foot canoe with experienced guides — no experience or reservation required.

name: Art of Manga at Brooklyn Museum
price: General admission (Manga Fan Pass $75 for unlimited entry + perks)
why: The first major exhibition in the Americas to explore manga as an art form — 600+ original drawings from beloved series including Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Ōoku: The Inner Chambers, and ONE PIECE. East Coast debut.

name: Open House New York (OHNY) Weekend 2026
time: October 16–18, 2026 (tickets release October 2; public reveal September 25)
venue: Citywide — 300 locations across all five boroughs
price: Ticketed (price TBD at Oct 2 release; membership gives early access)
why: NYC's annual festival of architecture and urban design — 300 buildings, facilities, and spaces normally closed to the public open for free or ticketed behind-the-scenes access. Teased sites include the Flatiron Building exterior tour with restoration architects, the NYC DOT Sign Shop in Maspeth, and the 1920s Con Edison East River Generating Station.

name: NY Transit Museum Bus Fest
why: Annual celebration of NYC's bus fleet — climb aboard vintage and modern buses, explore the evolution of public transit, meet MTA workers, and snap photos of historic vehicles with the Manhattan skyline as backdrop.

name: NY Transit Museum Vinyl Nights: Return to '76
venue: New York Transit Museum, Brooklyn Heights
why: 50th anniversary fundraiser event transforming the museum into a two-level dance party with analog vinyl — disco on the mezzanine, funk and hip-hop on the platform among vintage subway cars.

name: NY Transit Museum Nostalgia Ride to Green-Wood Cemetery
venue: Departs New York Transit Museum, Brooklyn Heights
why: Ride a vintage subway car to Green-Wood Cemetery for a guided tour of its famous permanent residents — Victorian-era actors, politicians, artists, and inventors — with time to picnic among the historic monuments.

name: NY Transit Museum Fly Away Redbirds Nostalgia Ride
venue: Departs Old South Ferry Station (normally closed)
why: Round-trip excursion on the beloved Redbird subway cars (in service 1959–2003), departing from the historic Old South Ferry station — closed to the public since 2017 — up through the Bronx.

name: MAS Grand Central Terminal Tours
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Ongoing guided tours of Grand Central Terminal led by MAS Docents — exploring Beaux-Arts architecture, hidden passages, the recently restored Main Concourse, and the building's history as a contested landmark.

name: The Weitzman Shoe Museum at New-York Historical Society
why: 600+ pairs of historic footwear from Stuart Weitzman and Jane Gershon Weitzman — shoes going back centuries, including Beyoncé boots designed by Weitzman himself, with interactive history and fashion stations.

name: New York: The Future of Cities — Advance Screening + Panel
why: Advance screening of highlights from acclaimed filmmaker Ric Burns's new two-part PBS documentary, followed by a panel discussion on the forces that have shaped New York in the 21st century and what history reveals about the city's future.

name: Wiseman's New York: Public vs. Private — Closing Panel
source: Architectural League of New York / UnionDocs
why: Closing panel for Wiseman's New York retrospective — Urban Omnibus Editor-in-Chief Mariana Mogilevich, critic K. Austin Collins, filmmaker Nilita Vachani, and scholar Genevieve Yue examine the structures behind what Frederick Wiseman captures on screen in his NYC films.

name: Architecture, Planning, and International Law: Building Postcarbon Futures
venue: The Architectural League of New York (TBD in-person location)
why: Free public panel on how international law intersects with architectural and planning practice in designing for a postcarbon future, from the Architectural League.

name: Journey of a Soca King: The Machel Montano Exhibition
why: Final days (closes Sep 12) of this exhibition celebrating soca legend Machel Montano — costumes, trophies, vinyl records, and artifacts tracing his lifelong contributions to soca music and Caribbean culture.

name: 9/11: Reclaiming Ground Zero — Screening & Talkback
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Dweck Center, Central Library
why: Screening of the new documentary 9/11: Reclaiming Ground Zero, followed by a conversation with director Josh Sabey, civic engagement scholar Carolyn Lukensmeyer, Dr. Sarah Sayeed, and architecture critic Michael Kimmelman about rebuilding Ground Zero.

name: Art as Care: Hospital Murals in Pediatric Healthcare — Panel Discussion
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Panel bringing together artists, hospital leaders, and advocates to examine what ambitious public art does in spaces where NYC's youngest patients receive care — tracing the line from WPA-era murals in children's wards to Keith Haring's hospital gift to evidence-based design today. Presented with the 'Another Wonderland' exhibition.

name: NYBG Climate Week NYC 2026: Nature Your City Keynote + Panel
price: Free (advance registration required at nybg.org; garden grounds free this day for Climate Week events)
why: Keynote address with leading urban ecologist Dr. Timon McPhearson followed by a panel on 'Nature Your City' — how urban greening and plant-based solutions create climate-resilient cities. Paired with a Farmers Market, partner organizations showcase, and garden exploration; grounds admission free this day.

name: NYBG 5K Fun Run
why: Scenic 3.1-mile road and trail course through the historic Thain Family Forest, one of NYC's largest old-growth forests, and past the Enid A. Haupt Conservatory — supporting NYBG's biodiversity research and climate work.

name: Brooklyn Craft Company September Workshops
time: Multiple dates/times starting September 13 (check brooklyncraftcompany.com for full schedule)
why: September lineup at this beloved Greenpoint craft studio: Macramé Plant Hanger (Sep 13), Sew a Jumpsuit (Sep 13), Intro to Garment Sewing: Free Range Slacks (starts Sep 14), Sock Knitting (Sep 15), 5-Week Sewing Course: Ilford Jacket (starts Sep 17), Knitting 102: Billie Bandana (Sep 23), and more.

name: Untapped Cities: Secrets of Grand Central Terminal Tour
why: Expert-led walking tour uncovering the hidden layers of Grand Central — from the remnants of a lost movie theater and former office-speakeasy to hidden tennis courts and the transit history behind the terminal.

name: Untapped Cities: Art Deco Icons of NYC Tour
time: Fridays at 4 PM and Sundays at 10 AM
venue: Midtown (meeting point at Chrysler Building area)
why: Recurring walking tour exploring the Chrysler Building, Rockefeller Center, and other Art Deco icons of midtown from a fresh architectural and historical perspective.
